newsitem.title: USA: Boston Fed chief does not see much wage pressures.
newsitem.headline: Boston Fed chief does not see much wage pressures.

text.p: The U.S. economy is not showing strong upward wage pressures despite a very low unemployment rate, said the president of the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston, Cathy Minehan.
"I don't think we're seeing a whole lot of wage pressures yet," she told reporters here following a conference on Social Security sponsored by the Federal Reserve Bank of Boston.
Minehan also said she expected the economy to show a more robust rate of growth in the second half of the year than the rate of growth expected for the second quarter.
Many Wall Street economists currently expect the U.S. second quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP) to post a substantially slower growth rate than the 5.8 percent surge seen in the first quarter.
"I don't think we're headed for the rest of the year to be as slow as the second quarter," the Boston Fed head said.
Minehan said her forecasts were based on expectations for continued low unemployment, high consumer confidence and rising income levels.
"All the components for a fairly solid rate of growth are there," Minehan said.
